title: 13 Employees Sold for $1 Billion #shorts
description:
In 2012, Facebook paid one billion dollars for Instagram, a photo app with thirteen employees and no revenue, only eighteen months after launch.
Follow for more stories of money made overnight.
first_comment: Would you have sold for $1 billion, or held on? Instagram is worth far more today 👇

lines.text: In 2012, a company with thirteen employees and zero revenue sold for one billion dollars.
It was a photo app called Instagram.
Its founder, Kevin Systrom, was twenty-eight.
He had launched it just eighteen months earlier.
Twenty-five thousand people signed up on day one.
Within a year, thirty million people were posting photos, and the servers barely survived.
Investors valued it at around five hundred million dollars.
And still, it had not made a single dollar.
But Mark Zuckerberg saw a threat: a rival that could steal his users.
In a few days, he offered one billion dollars.
Today, Instagram has over two billion users.
